entities.name: Hormizd II
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Hormizd II was the king (shah) of the Sasanian Empire, reigning for six years and five months from 303 to 309 CE. He succeeded his father Narseh and faced significant challenges in maintaining the empire's territorial integrity against various external threats.

As Hormizd II navigated the complexities of imperial politics, he implemented policies aimed at promoting economic growth and military expansion. His reign saw a period of relative stability, with the Sasanian Empire continuing to exert influence across its vast territories.

Despite these achievements, Hormizd II's legacy is often overshadowed by that of his predecessors and successors, who played more significant roles in shaping the empire's destiny.

The inscription on the Hormizd Bridge at Ctesiphon, dedicated to Hormizd II's son Shapur III, serves as a poignant reminder of his enduring presence in Sasanian history.
